sam: Heads-up — last night APAC peak (19:12-19:20 JST) we saw p99 jump and a short burst of 504s. Queue depth doubled, GPU-hour burn spiked ~2x. Anyone tracking root cause?
cheng: looked at traces — a lot of cold KV-cache misses + big network egress to object store. p95 stayed fine, p99 tail driven by a few long-running requests that hit cold KV + recompile path.
maria: can you drop a sample trace + the GPU-hour numbers for that window? also which model + batch size were serving?
sam: snippet below (sanitized), model=redwood-v2-13b, max_batch=64, avg_tokens=900. GPU-hours 00:08:00 * 12 nodes ~= 1.6 GPU-hours during spike. logs:
```
2024-06-18T19:12:05Z request id=abc123 latency=4.2s kv_miss=true net_egress=120MB
2024-06-18T19:12:07Z request id=def456 latency=5.8s kv_miss=true recompile=false
```
cheng: quick admit math we ran locally:`
```
# rough admit calc (tokens/s capacity model):
GPU_TOK_PER_SEC = 120000  # tokens per GPU-second (profiled)
avg_tokens_per_req = 900
target_util = 0.7  # keep headroom for p99
admit_per_sec = int((GPU_TOK_PER_SEC * target_util) / avg_tokens_per_req)
# = ~93 requests/sec per GPU
```
cheng: with max_batch=64 the effective concurrency pushes KV-cache churn; lowering batch reduces tail variance. also KV TTL set to 5m — too long for this hotspot.
lee: short-term mitigations: 1) prewarm + linear ramp 10m before window, 2) reduce max_batch to 32 for APAC routes during surge, 3) reduce KV TTL to 30s for the hot prefix, 4) enable soft-admit (drop low-priority requests) at p95->p99 thresholds.
jon: cost check — prewarming 10 gpus for 10m = (10 * 10m) = 100 gpu-min = 1.66 gpu-hours. run twice a day = 3.3 gpu-hours/day ~ weekly 23 gpu-hours. marginal cost acceptable vs 504s.
maria: longer term: add predictive headroom using traffic calendar, move hot KV to local SSDs in APAC region to cut egress and ms latency. also consider quantized v2-small fallback for non-critical routes (saves ~40% tokens/sec).
sam: agreeable. can we implement a staged plan: A) immediate change max_batch=32 and KV TTL=30s for hot prefixes B) prewarm scheduled job + soft-admit policy for this 10m window C) telemetry: add p99 breakdown by kv_miss + net_egress so we can measure impact. who owns A/B/C?
lee: I can own A (config change + canary tonight).
maria: I'll prototype local SSD hot-shard plan and perf test fallback model.
cheng: I'll add the admit curve sim and update the SLO dashboard slices. need a small script to recompute admit thresholds when avg_tokens changes.
sam: thanks — @lee please post canary results here. @deploy-bot please schedule prewarm job for 2024-06-19 19:00 JST with 10m ramp.
deploy-bot: scheduled job \"apac-prewarm-ramp\" for 2024-06-19T18:50:00Z -> 2024-06-19T19:10:00Z. :white_check_mark:
lee: canary started on canary cluster now, lowering max_batch to 32 for route /v1/chat-apac. will report p99 in 20m. :eyes:
sam: thanks team. will follow up after canary. :thumbsup:
